paper.title: Time-Varying Gaussian Process Bandits with Unknown Prior

settings.name_in_paper: Time-varying GP bandits with unknown prior
unmapped: The spatio-temporal function f(x,t) is a sample from a GP prior over X x [T] (time-varying evolution governed by the spatio-temporal kernel), not a variation-budget model
The true prior is unknown but the learner is given a finite set U of candidate GP priors (mean and kernel) containing it
Kernels bounded by 1 and prior means bounded on X
settings.definition_quote: We consider a problem setting where we wish to maximise an unknown, black-box and spatio-temporal function $f: \mathcal{X} \times [T] \to \mathbb{R}$ over some compact set $\mathcal{X} \subset \mathbb{R}^d$. ... $y_t = f(\bm{x}_t, t) + \epsilon_t$ by some i.i.d. Gaussian noise $\epsilon_t \sim \mathcal{N}(0, R^2)$ ... the available domain at each time step $\mathcal{X}_t \subseteq \mathcal{X}$ can change in an arbitrary manner, possibly chosen by an adversary. ... We assume that the black-box function and its evolution through time are governed by some prior, i.e., $f \sim p^\star(f)$ ... we are given access to a set of priors $\mathcal{U}$ ... that contains the true prior

algorithms.name: PE-GP-UCB (Prior Elimination GP-UCB)
requires_knowledge_of: Assumption 3.2 constants a^p, b^p, r (infinite X) or |X| (finite X)

symbols.B_tstar: beta_t^{p*} + max_{t'<=t*} sup_x |mu^{p*}(x,t')| + 1, where t* is the last iteration where a prior was rejected
symbols.beta_T: max over priors of confidence parameter beta_T^p
symbols.gamma_T: maximum information gain maximised over candidate priors, max_p gamma_T^p

conditions: f ~ p*(f) with p* in U
k^p <= 1 and prior means bounded for all p in U
if X infinite: Assumption 3.2 (X subset [0,r]^d compact convex, sample-path derivative tail bound with constants a^p,b^p)
tuning: finite X: beta_t^p = sqrt(2 log(2|X| pi^2 t^2/delta))
infinite X: beta_t^p = sqrt(2 log(3 pi^2 t^2/(2 delta)) + 2d log(d t^2 r b^p sqrt(log(3 d a^p/(2 delta)))))

source.label: theorem:noregret
source.quote: Let $f \sim p^*(f)$, $\epsilon_t \sim \mathcal{N}(0, R^2)$ for each $t$ and $p^* \in \mathcal{U}$ and denote $\gamma_T = \max_{p \in \mathcal{U}} \gamma_T^p$. Set $\xi_t = 2 R^2 \log \frac{|\mathcal{U}| \pi^2 t^2}{\delta}$ ... Then, Algorithm 1 with probability at least $1 - \delta$ achieves the cumulative regret of at most: R_T \le \mathcal{O} ( |\mathcal{U}|B_{t^\star} + \sqrt{|\mathcal{U}|\xi_T T} + \beta_T \sqrt{|\mathcal{U}|T \gamma}_{T} )

results.notes: Regret is against the per-round optimum over X_t (dynamic). Probability is over the GP prior sample and the noise. B_{t*} is a random quantity (Lemma 6.1 shows B_{t*}/T -> 0 a.s.). Proof gives explicit form 2|U|B_{t*} + 2 sqrt(xi_T |U| T) + 2 beta_T sqrt(C T |U| gamma_T). Parameters do not require T (anytime).

symbols.eps_tv: forgetting/time-variation parameter epsilon of the time-varying kernel (1-eps)^{|t-t'|/2}

conditions: all candidate priors use the (time-varying) squared exponential kernel

source.label: corollary:win
source.quote: Let all candidate priors utilise the squared exponential kernel, we then have that regret of PE-GP-UCB: $R_T = \Tilde{\mathcal{O}}( |\mathcal{U}| B_{t^\star} + \sqrt{|\mathcal{U}|}\max\{T\varepsilon^{1/6}, \sqrt{T}\})$

results.notes: Plugs MIG bound of Bogunovic et al. (2016) for time-varying SE kernel.

bound.expression: U_size*B_tstar + sqrt(U_size)*Max(T*eps_tv**((1 - c_mat)/(2*(3 - c_mat))), sqrt(T**(1 + c_mat)))

symbols.eps_tv: forgetting/time-variation parameter epsilon of the time-varying kernel

conditions: all candidate priors use the (time-varying) nu-Matern kernel

source.label: corollary:win
source.quote: Let all candidate priors utilise the $\nu$-Matern kernel, we then have that regret of PE-GP-UCB: $R_T = \Tilde{\mathcal{O}}(|\mathcal{U}| B_{t^\star} + \sqrt{|\mathcal{U}|}\max\{T\varepsilon^{\frac{1}{2} \frac{1 - c}{3 - c}}, \sqrt{T^{1+c}}\})$

results.notes: c defined in appendix as d(d+1)/(2nu+d(d+1)).

cited_results.setting_description: (Time-varying) GP bandits with known prior; Bayesian setting, regret w.h.p.
